newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Allies of South Africa's ANC attack new black elite.
newsitem.headline: Allies of South Africa's ANC attack new black elite.

text.p: South African communists and unionists allied to the ruling ANC said on Monday they were committed to socialism and warned against economic gain for a "small elite" of blacks.

The South African Communist Party (SACP) and the powerful Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) form an official alliance with President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress, but its strength has been tested by economic policy differences.
The ANC abandoned its commitment to socialism when it came to power in 1994 and has adopted markets-friendly policies, many of which Cosatu and the SACP oppose.

"Both SACP and Cosatu are convinced that a socialist perspective is essential for the advancing and deepening of democracy in our country," the two groups said in a joint statement issued after a bilateral meeting on Monday.
"Our class opponents are attempting to hijack the process of change in our country by encouraging a culture of self enrichment in the form of black economic empowerment for a small elite," they said.
Black investors have been buying key stakes in South Africa's white-dominated economy but critics say this will not help create sorely needed jobs for the unemployed.
The SACP and Cosatu said they were committed to their tripartite alliance with the ANC but said it needed a clear programme as the basis for going forward.
